function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool

This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run** example that creates a new Compute Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with:

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Image | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) |
| Machine type | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – you can change it) |
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (1 GPU) |
| Zone | `us-central1-a` (you can pick another zone) |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have the **Google Cloud SDK** (`gcloud`) installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled for your project.  
> * Your account/project must have the **Compute Admin** role (or equivalent) and enough quota for GPUs in the chosen zone.

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID with your actual project ID
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"

# Create a new VM named "rtx-a6000-demo" in us-central1-a
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=us-central1-a \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --service-account=default \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --image-family=focal-cloud \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=200GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-demo \
    --no-shielded-secure-boot \
    --no-shielded-vtpm \
    --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: add a startup script if needed
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100 \     # <-- replace with RTX A6000
```

> **NOTE:**  
> - GCP currently offers the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** and **T4** GPUs. The RTX A6000 is not available as a pre‑built accelerator. If you truly need an RTX A6000, you would typically use a custom image on a bare‑metal host or a different provider.  
> - If you do want an A100, replace the `--accelerator` line with:
>   ```bash
>   --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100
>   ```
> - If you want a T4 instead:
>   ```bash
>   --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-t4
>   ```

---

## 2️⃣ Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or via `curl`), here’s the full JSON payload you’d POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/focal-cloud",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "purpose": "demo"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
# Authenticate first
gcloud auth application-default login

# Get an OAuth token
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# Replace PROJECT_ID and ZONE appropriately
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Save the JSON above into a file called instance.json
cat >instance.json <<EOF
{ ... }   # paste the JSON payload here
EOF

# Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Task |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Verify GPU quota in the target zone (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:${ZONE}"`) |
| ✅ | Ensure the `nvidia-driver-installer` package is installed on the instance (you can add it to the startup script). |
| ✅ | Add firewall rules if you need external access to specific ports. |
| ✅ | Optionally, set a custom service account with only the permissions you actually need. |

---

### Final Note

Because the **RTX A6000** is not a standard Compute Engine accelerator, the examples above use the closest available GPU (Tesla A100). If you absolutely need an RTX A6000, consider:

* Using a **bare‑metal solution** (e.g., GCP Bare Metal Solution) where you can bring your own hardware.  
* Or switching to a provider that offers RTX A6000 GPUs (AWS, Azure, or specialized HPC providers).
